parsed.explanation: The combined regime is hostile at both levels. National passport/visa rules can refuse or scrutinize mismatched documents and expose a visitor to a fraud/lifetime-ineligibility finding; immigration custody has documented severe abuse. The division adds a public-facility statute covering state airports, government buildings, schools and prisons, enforced by on-site orders and criminal trespass if refused, though private businesses are excluded and the sole prosecution was dismissed. State identity-document and care rules compound the national regime. National hate-crime and employment protections and partial court injunctions are real but do not offset active traveller-facing facility and border exposures. This is High Risk, not Severe: no general criminalisation of trans identity and no execution pathway is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: National sex-marker restrictions; X markers not processed; discrepancies can lead to refusal and possible fraud/lifetime ineligibility. Division DMV treats marker mismatch as fraud.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding is not automatic and requires four elements; legal challenges and FAQ exist.
entry_documents.interaction: Border officer discretion can cascade from document mismatch to secondary inspection, refusal, or removal; state document rules compound national screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections practices include conversion-style measures; facility refusal can trigger criminal trespass.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some national executive orders are enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity, but custody protections are thin.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy can move a traveller into immigration detention; a facility order can move them into local criminal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law bars gender-congruent restroom/changing use in state and local government buildings, including airports, schools, parks and prisons; refusal to leave is criminal trespass. National rules bar funding for congruent single-sex facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses are outside the division statute; limited exemptions apply; the sole prosecution was dismissed and the statute was never substantively tested.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor using a state airport or government building must use a birth-sex facility or risk an order to leave and possible trespass charge; national facilities add exclusion.

care_services.exposure: Division law restricts gender-affirming care for minors and imposes adult barriers, insurance limits and conscience refusal; national policy pressures minor care and insurance coverage.
care_services.protection: Court injunctions blocked some care provisions; local protections exist in parts of the division.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing HRT or emergency care may face refusal or record mismatch; a trans minor travelling with a guardian faces compounded care restrictions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism rhetoric names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice guidance creates rewards and scrutiny; executive orders target 'gender ideology'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The counterterrorism strategy states mere disagreement is not targeted; courts have enjoined several orders; national hate-crime law covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Raises scrutiny and discovery risk around advocacy or visible trans status, but does not by itself criminalise a visitor's identity.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division bans care for minors; national orders threaten prosecution over social transition; facility law covers schools and public buildings; custody rules can be used against parents.
minors_guardians.protection: Some care provisions are enjoined; local nondiscrimination protections cover part of the population.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor with a guardian faces facility exclusion and care denial in the division; the guardian may face official scrutiny over a child's transition.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented rate of 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k per year and a 'Do Not Travel' label; division hate-crime law excludes gender identity; police enforce facility restrictions.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; local nondiscrimination laws cover about 55% of the population; no documented police extortion pattern.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence risk is independent of law, but thin state hate-crime coverage and police enforcement of facility rules reduce recourse after an incident.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facility statute never substantively tested; care litigation unresolved; border fraud policy challenged; travel advisories are dated; airport application is undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked some national orders; civil-liberties FAQ and national hate-crime/employment protections exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow and uncertain; a visitor cannot rely on them at the border, in a facility encounter, or in custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Comparable low-level detention and extortion uncertainty, but this jurisdiction adds a state-imposed facility criminal statute and documented severe immigration-custody abuse. It is somewhat worse than 0.25-A, though the record does not show a repeated extortion cycle.

0.35-A involves invasive border screening and denial of entry without detention. Here the national fraud/lifetime-ineligibility pathway and the division's facility trespass exposure make the operative regime materially harsher, placing it below 0.35-A.

0.55-A shows an ombudsman securing release and a charter barring prolonged holds. This jurisdiction has no comparable traveller-facing remedy for facility exclusion or border document refusal, so it sits well below 0.55-A.

parsed.synthesis: National document screening and the division's facility statute form one operative system: a passport mismatch can lead to refusal, secondary inspection or a fraud finding, while a state airport or government building can require birth-sex facility use backed by trespass. Private businesses are outside the division statute and national hate-crime/employment protections exist, but they do not reach border discretion or on-site facility enforcement. Custody and care exposures are severe if triggered. The result is High Risk.
